---
name: git-bash-msys-ad-stall
description: "Why Git Bash randomly dies on this machine (add_item errno 1) — AD lookup blows past MSYS2's 15s spinlock; fix is nsswitch files-only + shell:powershell hooks"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1af2d0a6-e25b-4097-a3e5-e0f45a6e5d14
  modified: 2026-08-03T03:50:43.299Z
---

Git Bash on this machine intermittently dies at startup with
`bash.exe: *** fatal error - add_item ("\??\C:\Program Files\Git", "/", ...) failed, errno 1`
(exit 0xC0000005). This is the real explanation behind the global CLAUDE.md rule
"prefer PowerShell, Bash fails silently on this Windows setup."

**Mechanism (measured 2026-08-02):** MSYS2 builds its shared-memory mount table once,
guarded by a spinlock in `shared.cc` with a hard **15-second timeout**. Past that, waiting
processes enter the critical section anyway, `mountinfo.init()` runs twice, and `add_item("/")`
aborts. Observed directly: three consecutive launches took **15.17–15.20 s** then died — the
timeout itself.

**Trigger:** machine is domain-joined to `baylor.edu`; `C:\Program Files\Git\etc\nsswitch.conf`
ships `passwd: files db` with **no `/etc/passwd`**, so every bash launch resolves identity over
LDAP. Slow DC → >15 s → crash. Bursty, not constant: ~0.5% of launches normally (0/500 when the
DC is fast, `id` = 421 ms), but once one process wedges, *every* concurrent launch fails. Claude
Code fires 3–4 Stop hooks simultaneously, landing right in that window.

**Verified non-causes:** not the `bin\bash.exe` wrapper (0/700 vs 4/788, not significant), not
concurrency alone (0/48 parallel), not mandatory ASLR (NOTSET), not a username with a period
(`Eric_Rash` has none), not duplicate msys DLLs (one only).

**Fixes applied:** hooks in `settings.json` + `settings.local.json` now use `"shell": "powershell"`
(a real hook field; Windows defaults to bash). Switching shell **requires rewriting POSIX commands** —
`[ ! -f X ] || node X` is a PowerShell syntax error; use `if (Test-Path X) { node X }`. stdin JSON
passes through the wrapper fine.

**Root-cause fix — APPLIED 2026-08-02** via `~/.claude/scripts/fix-msys-ad-stall.ps1` (run elevated):
static `/etc/passwd` (13 entries, incl. SYSTEM for scheduled tasks) + `/etc/group` (29) generated
with `mkpasswd -l -c` / `mkgroup -l -c` — never `-d`, which enumerates the whole domain — and
nsswitch set to `passwd: files` / `group: files` / `db_enum: builtin`. uid/gid and
`HOME=/c/Users/eric_rash` unchanged. Verified 550 consecutive clean launches (400 sequential +
150 concurrent), max 2.3 s. Backup `nsswitch.conf.bak-*` in `Git\etc`; `-Rollback` to undo.

**Verification gotcha that cost a run:** comparing the whole `id` string false-fails. Adding
`/etc/group` legitimately *enriches* the output — group names start resolving and the full
supplementary list appears (`gid=1049089` → `gid=1049089(Domain Users) groups=...,545(Users)`).
Compare **uid + primary gid only**. Also: an elevated shell's token includes `Administrators`,
so `id` output differs between elevated and normal shells — not a regression. And any script that
verifies by shelling out to bash must **retry**, since bash is the thing that intermittently
crashes; a single transient failure otherwise triggers a spurious rollback of a good config.

Gotcha when testing: `id`/`mkpasswd` reporting "command not found" from `bash -c` is just PATH
(non-login shell inherits Windows PATH) — use `bash -lc`, not evidence the tools are missing.

input.summary: The core hook chain works. All 13 hooks wired in ~/.claude/settings.json point at files that exist and pass a syntax check, uv, dcg, node and python3 all resolve, and the session-start, transcript-capture, skill-router, dcg and autopush hooks show recent successful runs. The main exposure is in permissions: a bare "Bash" allow rule plus auto mode with both bypass prompts turned off, and 129 allow rules, of which 20 point at Windows paths and 57 are one-off commands. The other problems are drift: plugin copies synced from the claude.ai account escape Eric's disables and quieting hooks (GitHub MCP fails with a 400 every session, and the superpowers injection still fires), the Codex copy of keystone-unified-snapshot.js is behind, a LIFEOS hooks.json with 60 entries and 50 orphan hook files is still on disk, and the skill-router roster is a month stale.

findings.title: Bare "Bash" allow rule with defaultMode auto and both permission bypass prompts suppressed
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.allow[0] = "Bash"; defaultMode "auto"; skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt true; skipAutoPermissionPrompt true; useAutoModeDuringPlan true; autoMode.allow carries a standing gh pr merge approval. 95 of the 129 allow rules are Bash(...) rules that the bare "Bash" already covers. Also allowed: Bash(launchctl:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(python:*), Bash(python3:*), Bash(node:*), Bash(npm install:*), Bash(gh api *), Bash(vercel env:*), Bash(vercel deploy:*). settings.local.json adds Bash(claude:*), Bash(npm:*) and Bash(powershell.exe:*). The only code-level Bash guard is the dcg PreToolUse hook (verified: it denies `git reset --hard`). The permission-gate hook is shadow-only and never blocks.
findings.impact: If the auto-mode classifier misses something, or a session runs in a mode that honors allow rules literally, any shell command runs without a prompt. That includes launchctl changes, global installs, git force operations and nested `claude` runs. dcg only catches its own pattern packs. I did not verify how the auto classifier treats a bare Bash rule. TypeSafe STATUS says the classifier still blocks some sends, so this is exposure, not a confirmed bypass. settings.json syncs to the Windows desktop-app sessions through dotclaude.
findings.fix: Remove the bare "Bash" rule and the broad interpreter and launchctl rules. Keep narrow read-only patterns, and leave the broad ones to the auto classifier plus dcg. Decide on purpose whether skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt is still wanted.

findings.title: GitHub MCP fails with a 400 every session even though Eric disabled the GitHub plugin today
findings.evidence: This session's harness reported: plugin:github:github (400) "Authorization header is badly formatted". settings.json and settings.local.json both set "github@claude-plugins-official": false (toggled off in dotclaude commit f736ab5, 2026-10-22). But ~/.claude/plugins/synced/507a61e7-.../8cc1afaf-f7a8-48ad-be6f-c3d096b6329e (plugin.json name "github", marketplace anthropic-plugin-directory) ships a .mcp.json with Authorization "Bearer ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}", and GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN is unset in the environment.
findings.impact: A failed MCP connection on every session start, plus a misleading 'server failed' notice. The disable Eric applied today has no effect on the copy synced from his claude.ai account.
findings.fix: Turn the GitHub plugin off in the claude.ai account plugin settings, which removes the synced copy. Or, if he wants it, supply a PAT through the Keychain-backed env. gh CLI already covers GitHub work.

findings.title: superpowers-quiet.mjs misses the claude.ai-synced superpowers copy, so the 1% injection still fires
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/hooks/superpowers-quiet.mjs patches only ~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/*. Both cache versions (6.4.1, 7.0.0) were patched on Oct 16 (hooks.json is 18 bytes, .orig saved). The synced copy ~/.claude/plugins/synced/507a61e7-.../6ba53849-...~g2 (superpowers 6.4.2) still has a SessionStart entry in hooks/hooks.json. Session 61b98418 (2026-10-22T17:35Z) recorded the SessionStart:startup hook "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.cmd" session-start injecting "<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT> You have superpowers...". The synced 6.4.2 copy is the only one with an unpatched SessionStart, so it is the likely source.
findings.impact: The emphatic 'MUST invoke skills' text that Eric deliberately removed (CLAUDE.md: skills are tools, not a gate) comes back in at least some sessions. It also points to two superpowers versions being loaded side by side.
findings.fix: Turn off the account-synced superpowers plugin on claude.ai (7.0.0 is already installed locally), or widen superpowers-quiet.mjs to scan plugins/synced/*/* entries whose plugin.json name is superpowers.

findings.title: Codex copy of keystone-unified-snapshot.js has drifted from the Claude copy
findings.evidence: diff ~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js ~/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js: the Codex copy (Sep 13, 3399 B) lacks summarizeErrors(), `summarize: true` and the ~/DEV vs ~/Desktop/DEV fallback that the Claude copy has (Sep 29, 5205 B). ~/.codex/hooks.json wires it: SessionStart `node '/Users/kristinarash/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js'`. findings.title: settings.local.json is tracked in git, so Windows-only impeccable hooks and Windows rules load on the Mac
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/.gitignore whitelists `!/settings.local.json`, and dotclaude tracks it. It wires 5 impeccable hook entries (PostToolUse Edit|Write|MultiEdit and Edit|Write, two Stop entries with 30 s timeouts, one SessionStart), all calling C:\\Users\\eric_rash\\.claude\\skills\\impeccable\\scripts\\impeccable. The entries are duplicated, so an Edit matches twice and Stop runs twice. Allow rules include Bash(winget install:*), Bash(powershell.exe:*) and Bash(claude:*). Memory project_git-bash-msys-ad-stall.md says these hooks use "shell": "powershell", but neither file has a "shell" field now (count 0).

A file named 'local' that actually syncs between machines invites more cross-machine leakage. The memory note is stale against the live config.
findings.fix: Stop tracking settings.local.json (remove the whitelist line and `git rm --cached`), or move the impeccable hooks into a Windows-only file. Dedupe the entries. Update or retire the git-bash memory.

findings.title: 129 allow rules, mostly stale: Windows paths, task IDs, one-off commands, multiline junk

findings.title: LIFEOS hooks.json (60 entries) and 50 orphan .hook.ts/.sh files remain in ~/.claude/hooks
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/hooks/hooks.json (Jul 8) defines 60 hook entries across PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PermissionRequest/ConfigChange, etc. They run `bun` .hook.ts scripts, LIFEOS/TOOLS/MergeSettings.ts, and http hooks to localhost:31337, where nothing is listening (lsof shows no listener). No settings file wires any of them. 50 *.hook.ts/*.hook.sh files plus handlers/ and lib/ are orphans. They are executable, bun exists at ~/.bun/bin/bun, and dotclaude tracks them (80 tracked files under hooks/). They are mirrored into ~/.codex/hooks. ~/.claude/settings.json.lifeos-backup-1783558458907 is from the same install.
findings.impact: This is inert today, but it is a loaded config. If anything merges it (LIFEOS MergeSettings.ts, or a plugin-style loader), 60 hooks, including SettingsBackport and IdentityToSettingsSync, which rewrite settings, start firing on every tool call. It also confuses anyone debugging hooks and bloats the two-copies diff.
findings.fix: Move hooks.json, the *.hook.ts/.sh files, handlers/, lib/ and README.md into ~/.claude/_to_delete or an archive outside hooks/ in both ~/.claude and ~/.codex, then remove them from dotclaude.

findings.title: Skill-router roster is frozen at Sep 21 and misses newer skills; every prompt goes to api.typesafe.ai
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/skill-router/roster.json (Sep 21, 149 skills). Local skills missing from it: articulation-skill, before-building, decision-audit, decisions, room-cli, where-was-i. findings.known_where: Prompt egress was accepted as a design choice in ~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md:353 ('Accepted, not resolved: the first 500 characters of every prompt now go to api.typesafe.ai'). Roster staleness is not recorded.

findings.title: Credentials, the TypeSafe key file and the permission-gate hook code are world-writable (0666)
findings.evidence: stat: ~/.claude/.credentials.json -rw-rw-rw-; ~/.claude/typesafe.env -rw-rw-rw-; ~/.claude/permission-gate/{shadow_hook.py,rules.py,sanitize.py,shadow.jsonl} -rw-rw-rw-. shadow_hook.py runs on every Bash/MCP/WebFetch/SendMessage/Artifact call. Several settings.json.bak* files are also 0666. Mitigation: kristinarash (uid 501) is the only local account and the home dir is 0750.
findings.impact: Low exposure on a single-user Mac. But any process running as another uid in group staff could read the OAuth tokens or swap code into a hook that runs on every tool call. The pattern looks like a carry-over from the Windows import.
findings.fix: chmod 600 ~/.claude/.credentials.json ~/.claude/typesafe.env; chmod 644 ~/.claude/permission-gate/*.py; chmod 600 the settings backups.

findings.title: session-autopush can run past its 60 s budget, and parallel SessionEnd runs race on one repo
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/hooks/session-autopush.js says 'worst case about 50s, inside the 60s timeout', but its per-step git timeouts are rev-parse/status 15 s each, add 30, commit 60, fetch 20, rebase 30 and push 45, which together far exceed 60 s. ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-2026-10-20 has three identical lines within 80 ms: 'session-autopush: DEV: not pushed, fetch failed (offline?): error: git-remote-https died of signal 9'. Only one success line is in autopush.log since the hook was added on 10-19.
findings.impact: If the harness kills the hook during `git rebase`, the repo can be left mid-rebase. Concurrent runs on the same repo can collide on index.lock. The signal 9 suggests the processes were killed rather than offline. Failures do surface in .errors.log, so nothing fails silently.
findings.fix: Take a lock file per repo (skip if one is held), cap the total runtime under 55 s, and treat a signal-killed fetch as a skip rather than an offline error.

findings.title: Permission-gate shadow log grows without bound, and its planned review is a month overdue
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/permission-gate/shadow.jsonl: 4.6 MB, 15,630 lines since 2026-09-22. Verdicts: residue 9,690, run 5,614, review 286, block 41, plus 1 unparseable line. There is no rotation. TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md:445 says 'Watch the shadow log... After a week or two, count residue'. The staged copy matches the repo except for CRLF line endings.
findings.impact: A hook that runs on every tool call collects data nobody reads, and 62% of calls fall into 'residue', which the rules don't classify. Disk use is small.
findings.fix: Do the planned residue review, then either promote the gate or remove the PreToolUse entry. Add size-based rotation.

findings.title: skillOverrides has 150 entries, many naming skills that no longer exist
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/settings.json skillOverrides: 150 entries (109 off, 40 name-only, 1 user-invocable-only). Unprefixed names with no ~/.claude/skills dir include LIFEOS-era skills (Telos, Council, RedTeam, Fabric, LifeOS, Daemon, WorldThreatModel, ...) and pp-flight-goat, pp-movie-goat, pp-recipe-goat. Some unprefixed names may match plugin skills, so the exact dead count was not established.
findings.impact: Clutter makes it hard to see which overrides actually shape the skill list.
findings.fix: Prune overrides for skills that are not installed. Keep only those that match a skill in the current listing.

findings.title: Backup and log cruft: 14 settings backups, 21 temp_git dirs, an ever-growing heal log
findings.evidence: ~/.claude has 14 settings*.json backups (236 KB), dating from May 18 to Oct 22, including settings-backup-r1mu_1t3.json and settings.json.lifeos-backup-1783558458907. ~/.claude/plugins/cache has 21 leftover temp_git_* dirs (Oct 11 onward). ~/.claude/context-mode/heal-partial-install.log is 579 KB / 3,242 lines, appending 'skipped: not-partial' lines every session start. context-mode/hook-errors.log and sessionstart-debug.log are stale Windows logs (last written Oct 6, C:/Users/eric_rash paths). findings.title: session-autopush can run past its 60 s budget, and parallel SessionEnd runs race on one repo

Only one success line is in autopush.log since the hook was added on 10-19.
findings.impact: If the harness kills the hook during `git rebase`, the repo can be left mid-rebase. Concurrent runs on the same repo can collide on index.lock. The signal 9 suggests the processes were killed rather than offline. Failures do surface in .errors.log, so nothing fails silently.
findings.fix: Take a lock file per repo (skip if one is held), cap the total runtime under 55 s, and treat a signal-killed fetch as a skip rather than an offline error.

findings.title: Bare "Bash" allow rule with defaultMode auto and both permission bypass prompts suppressed
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.allow[0] = "Bash"; defaultMode "auto"; skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt true; skipAutoPermissionPrompt true; useAutoModeDuringPlan true; autoMode.allow carries a standing gh pr merge approval. 95 of the 129 allow rules are Bash(...) rules that the bare "Bash" already covers. Also allowed: Bash(launchctl:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(python:*), Bash(python3:*), Bash(node:*), Bash(npm install:*), Bash(gh api *), Bash(vercel env:*), Bash(vercel deploy:*). settings.local.json adds Bash(claude:*), Bash(npm:*) and Bash(powershell.exe:*). The only code-level Bash guard is the dcg PreToolUse hook (verified: it denies `git reset --hard`). The permission-gate hook is shadow-only and never blocks.
findings.impact: If the auto-mode classifier misses something, or a session runs in a mode that honors allow rules literally, any shell command runs without a prompt. That includes launchctl changes, global installs, git force operations and nested `claude` runs. dcg only catches its own pattern packs. I did not verify how the auto classifier treats a bare Bash rule. TypeSafe STATUS says the classifier still blocks some sends, so this is exposure, not a confirmed bypass. settings.json syncs to the Windows desktop-app sessions through dotclaude.
findings.fix: Remove the bare "Bash" rule and the broad interpreter and launchctl rules. Keep narrow read-only patterns, and leave the broad ones to the auto classifier plus dcg. Decide on purpose whether skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt is still wanted.

findings.fix: Stop tracking settings.local.json (remove the whitelist line and `git rm --cached`), or move the impeccable hooks into a Windows-only file. Dedupe the entries. Update or retire the git-bash memory.
